breakdown.description: 300 nm light has photon energy of about 4.13 eV, below a work function of 4.8 eV, so photoemission cannot occur.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification correctly uses 240 nm light (matching the ground truth) instead of the incorrect 300 nm light from the incomplete prompt. With 240 nm light, the photon energy is hc/λ = 1240/240 ≈ 5.17 eV, which exceeds the 4.8 eV work function, making photoelectric emission physically possible. The agent also removed the erroneous claim of 0.8 eV maximum kinetic energy and instead asks to determine whether emission occurs by comparing photon energy to the work function.
